newsitem.title: UK: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week In Review.
newsitem.headline: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week In Review.

text.p: This is Reuters' look back at the major developments in the air cargo industry in the week February 7 - February 14.
**FEBRUARY 7**
DUBLIN - Irish cut-price airline Ryanair unveiled details of new service to Paris and Brussels which it says undercut competition by 50 percent.
MOSCOW - Volga-Dnepr airline company says the central Russian city of Ulyanovsk has approved a project for a customs free zone at Ulyanovsk international airport.
ZAGRED - Croatian flag carrier Croatia airlines says it bought 12 CFM 56 engines worth $60 million from a French-American supplier CFM International.
FRANKFURT - Lufthansa says it is negotiating with British Midland on a possible cooperation agreement but declined to give further details.
LONDON - MSAS Cassin, part of MSAS Cargo International says it has opened a new office at Belfast International airport in Northern Ireland.
BRUSSELS - A BA official says it has not yet decided whether to release slots at London's Heathrow airport to win UK regulatory approval for its proposed alliance with American Airlines.
AMSTERDAM - Dutch airfreight truckers says the French government's ban on weekend road haulage traffic starting on March 28 was "bad for all hauliers."
LONDON - Davies Turner Air Cargo says it has invested in a new large X-ray machine at its London Heathrow airfreight hub to meet tougher security regulations applying to the airfreight industry.
FRANKFURT - The airport authority says Cologne airport increased air cargo volumes by 11.5 percent to 356,290 tonnes in 1996.
PARIS - MAS says it will increase its ex-Paris cargo rates by five percent, effective March 1.
MIAMI - Speakers at an air cargo conference urged airports and cargo executives need to do a better job telling the public about the economic benefits of the industry.
MONTREAL - Air France says it will move its cargo handling to Dorval airport once passenger flights begin using the airport in May.

WASHINGTON - A National Transportation Safety Board official says it will investigate this week's accident off the New Jersey coast involving a charted Boeing 727 airliner and two Air National Guard F-16 fighters.
LISBON - TAP says that it might sue top-selling author Michael Crichton over an air safety thriller in which it refers to "inept" maintenance at a company he calls "Air Portugal".
MADRID - Iberia says it closed 1996 with consolidated profit of around 3.5 billion pesetas.
FRANKFURT - Flughafen Frankfurt/Main says it is in initial talks about taking a stake of up to 30 percent in Hanover airport.
LONDON - BA says it took delivery from Boeing of the first longer-range version of the 777.

BUCHAREST - A top official says Romania's new government is relaunching a restructuring programme, headed by aircraft purchases for the state airline Tarom SA, but privatisation is not a priority for the moment.
LONDON - Eva Air, says it is to move into a new official European headquarters in London on February 24.
MIAMI - Angelo Pusateri, president-cargo, Virgin Atlantic Airways says airports have to start thinking like business partners and better serve their cargo airlines.
**FEBRUARY 8**
KUWAIT - The civil aviation directorate says Kuwait air cargo volumes rose 15 percent in January to 11,478 tonnes compared to the same period 1996.
WASHINGTON - CNN television reported the U.S. FAA has ordered all airlines operating Boeing 747 and 757 aircraft to begin making regular inspections of fuel pumps.
LOME - The West African Development Bank says it has agreed a 4.27 billion franc loan for Mali to help it extend the runway and improve facilities at Timbuktu airport.
AMSTERDAM - NRC Handelsblad newspaper says KLM will shed around 960 jobs from a total of 22,000 over the next three years as part of its Focus 2000 restructuring programme.
**FEBRUARY 10**
HONG KONG - Cathay says it expects to spend up to Us$6 billion on aircraft acquisitions for delivery from now until 2003.
LONDON - BA announced record profits which it says were boosted by increased traffic and cost-cutting, but a sharp rise in jet fuel prices hit operating profits.
* BA chief executive Robert Ayling says it plans to make a progress report on its campaign to find a billion pounds of annual cost savings when it reports full-year results in May.

NEW YORK - The Wall Street Journal says a White House commission wants billions of dollars more to be spent to enhance aviation security and speed the improvement of the nation's air-traffic control system.
ROME - Forli airport authority says scheduled air cargo traffic at Forli airport fell to 2,090 tonnes in 1996 from 2,133 the previous year.
STOCKHOLM - Lufthansa Cargo says it would start a five times a week freighter operation this week from Helsinki to Copenhagen.
ZURICH - Airport authority figures show global cargo traffic handled at Zurich airport in 1996 was up 1.4 percent on the previous year at 445,640 tonnes.
ARLINGTON - USAir says that it and BA were adding two new code share cities, Hamburg and Cologne/Bonn, effective March 5.
FRANKFURT - Lufthansa says it named Frederick Reid to head up its scheduled airline passenger unit which is due to come into being from April this year.
NEW DELHI - A senior government official says India is inching towards approval of a landmark proposal from the Tata Group to set up a domestic airline in partnership with SIA.
LONDON - A British Petroleum marketing official says airlines exposed to volatile fluctuations in jet fuel prices may reassess their risk management after a sharp spike last summer.

HONG KONG - Industry sources says what is seen as the start of a top management reshuffle within Hong Kong's airlines linked to its handover to China took place with Stanley Hui taking up his new position as head of Hong Kong Dragon Airlines.

LONDON - ANA Aviation Services says a new palletised airfreight connection between the Middle East and West Africa will be offered from next month following the signing of an interline agreement by Air Gabon and DAS Air.
WASHINGTON - The White House says the Federal Mediation Service has become involved in seeking to avert a strike by pilots at American Airlines and it will watch the talks closely.
FRANKFURT - The Germany airports association (ADV) says air cargo exports from Germany grew 6.5 percent to 1,011,904 tonnes in 1996.
* ADV says imports to Germany rose 5.1 percent to 919,382 tonnes in 1996.
* ADV says air cargo flown to and from Germany rose 6.9 percent in December 1996 to 175,998.
* ADV says total air cargo flown to and from Germany rose 5.7 percent to 1,985,282 tonnes in 1996.
* ADV says the Germany air passenger market grew 2.6 percent to 113.25 million passengers in 1996.

KIEV - A government spokesman says the Ukrainian government has ordered a cut in the number of airports serving international routes because it cannot afford to pay customs and passport control officers.
PARIS - United Airlines says its decision to introduce a Boeing 777 aircraft on its daily Paris-San Francisco from July 1997 will mean more cargo capacity is available on the route.

ROME - Air industry sources says a meeting of key local authority, airline and union representatives was due to take place on February 17 in Milan to study the transfer of operations to Malpensa airport from the city's other airport at Linate.
MOSCOW - FedEx says it has lowered its rates from Russian to all destinations worldwide.
ROME - Alitalia Cargo says it had signed an agreement with Formula One Constructors' Association to ship 11 racing cars competing in the 1997 Formula One Grand Prix to Melbourne.
FRANKFURT - Dresden airport authority says Tatarstan Airlines has launched a weekly flight from Kazan, capital of the Russian republic of Tatarstan, to Dresden.

PARIS - The Semaine Internationale du Transport et de La Logistique(SITL), an annual international freight transport and logistics conference will take place at the Parc des Expositions de Paris-Nord Villepinte exhibition centre, between March 18.21 1997.
LONDON - The Wilson Group, the air and seafreight division of the BTL Group, says it has acquired Ballauf Air, an airfreight company specialising in international logistics packages.
* Lufthansa figures show UK business travel to Eastern Europe is at an all time high, with an increase in passenger figures of 23 percent in the last six months of 1996.
NEW YORK - TWA says it initiated a hiring freeze, but says the plan would not affect pilots or "frontline" employees.
ATLANTA - Delta Air Lines says Varig Brazillian Airlines ended a code-share agreement that began in 1994.

* Delta says its spring 1997 schedule changes are expected to improve operating performance and support Delta's long-term strategy to build on its operating performance and support Delta's long-term strategy to build on its competitive strengths in its major hubs.

WASHINGTON - A federal court gave the Environmental Protection Agency an additional three weeks to issue new air quality standards, giving the public more time to weigh in on the EPA's controversial proposal.
**FEBRUARY 11**
LONDON - A British newspapers says American Airlines and British Airways are considering ways to start cooperating despite continued regulatory hurdles to a formal alliance.

SAN FRANCISCO - San Francisco's Board of Supervisors approved a United Airlines' lease at San Francisco airport after the two sides compromised on whether the airline must offer benefits to unmarried partners of its employees.
BANGKOK - A government spokesman says Thailand's Transport and Communications Ministry has recommended the controversial $4 billon Nong Ngu Hao airport project to be delayed.
* A government minister says the Thai Cabinet decided to review further the feasibility of building a second Bangkok airport at Nonmg Ngu Hao in the eastern outskirts of the capital.
MANILA - Philippine Airlines says it expects losses of "more or less" two billion pesos in the current fiscal year ending March 31, 1997.
JOHANNESBURG - Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau says South Africa has decided to offer 49 percent of state-run Sun Air to foreign buyers, instead of the 25 percent initially planned.
TORONTO - American Airlines, facing a Saturday strike deadline by its 10,000 pilots, says it will keep accepting cargo right up to Friday if it can be delivered before the threatened walkout.
PARIS - Air France Cargo says it is to raise some tariffs for cargo leaving France by between three and eight percent on March 1.
MANILA - Philippine Airlines officials says it is expected to post profits in 1988 or in 1999 after three years of mounting losses.
HARARE - A top industry official says cargo movements along the Zimbabwe-Beira road/rail corridor rose by 11 percent in 1996.
PARIS - Airbus confirmed GE Aircraft Engines will not build the GEXX engines for Airbus's planned stretched versions of its A340 plane.
FRANKFURT - German air space controllers says 24 near-misses in German airspace were reported in 1996, compared to 23 the year before.
PARIS - DHL France says 1996 turnover grew to 945 million francs from 841 million France the previous year.
BRUSSELS - BA chief executive Robert Ayling refused to comment on the substance of a meeting with European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert.
LONDON - BAA figures show the U.S. was the top origin and destination for air cargo imports and exports through BAA airports during April to December 1996.
* BAA says air cargo traffic at its seven airports in the nine months to December 1996 rose to 1.12 million tonnes or up 5.2 percent from the same period 1995.
FRANKFURT - Lufthansa Cargo vice-president Joachim Haas, says it will raise ex-Europe cargo rates by five to nine percent from March 1.
* Haas says it was considering dropping common air cargo rates from all German airports in favour of modular service-orientated prices.
* Haas says it has introduced a new global cargo management computer system and will phase in freight barcoding worldwide this year.
ATHENS - Olympic Airways says it has retained management consulting firms McKinsey & Company and Plant to help it on a project to improve competitiveness.

CAPE TOWN - Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad says South Africa is negotiating with China to obtain overflying rights for flights to Japan because of the decision to break diplomatic ties with Taiwan.

PARIS - Royal Brunei Airlines says it was looking to appoint a Paris-based GSA in preparation for the launch of a twice-weekly Boeing 767-300 passenger service between Charles de Gaulle and Brunei Darussalam later this year.
* Intra-European express company, Axor, a subsidiary of French Group, Jet Services, says it was planning to put a bigger aircraft on its nightly Liege-Paris CDG all-cargo service.

GENEVA - IATA director general says proposed reforms of European air traffic management, due to be passed this week, would give airlines and passengers a raw deal and fail to resolve congestion bottlenecks.

MIAMI - Industry officials says shippers and air cargo executives were pushing through about the same amount of Valentine's flowers this year as last, despite problems in the two biggest flower exporting countries.
FRANKFURT - Lufthansa Cargo senior vice-president Joachim Haas, says it sees only moderate growth for its European air cargo business in 1997.
* BA cargo manager Central Europe, Mark Gardiner says it will raise ex-Germany air cargo rates by up to 10 percent from March 1.
* Gardiner says poor quality standards at Heathrow have hit BA World Cargo sales in Germany.
PARIS - French courier operator, Chronopost, says it would be opening dedicated facilities at Marseille airport towards end-1997.
AMSTERDAM - Martinair proves that romance is not dead as it flies an extra 200 tonnes of flowers into Europe for Valentine's Day.

ROME - Alitalia says it will establish an operations units in Milan during April to coordinate flight operations and crew schedules, ahead of the move to Milan's Malpensa airport from the city's other airport at Linate.
ROME - Italian manufacturer Alenia says it will receive a stake in Airbus in exchange for assets.
WARSAW - PAP news agency says a company managing the small international Pyrzowice airport near the southern city of Krakow opened a new cargo terminal there.
DENVER - United Airlines says that it would be unfortunate if what it called "baseless charges" levelled against it by a competitor led to increased government interference in the airline industry.
* United inaugurated its Denver to Las Vegas and Denver to Phoenix shuttle service.
NEW YORK - American Airlines could permantly lose market share in Chicago and other key cities if pilots strike the airline this weekend.
**FEBRUARY 12**
DUBAI - English-language daily Gulf News reported Finland is trying to establish trade and cargo links with the UAE to cash in on the rich markets of the former Soviet Union.
NEW YORK - The New York Times say a White House commission is expected to release a report that sets a goal of cutting the rate of airline accidents by 80 percent.
ROME - Italian treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi says Alitalia is expected to see 1996 losses of around $790 million.
* Palermo airport says total air cargo traffic in 1996 rose 6.4 percent to 4,603, against 1995 figures.
* BAA spokesman says it is set to take a 65 percent stake in Capodichino airport in Naples, the third biggest in Italy.
FRANKFURT - Dutch airfreight company Rutges says it has won a ground handling contract for Nippon Cargo Airlines at Frankfurt airport.
WARSAW - Poland's national airline LOT SA flew 2.03 million people last year, up 10.5 percent from 1995 and transported 22,700 tonnes of air cargo, up 19 percent.
LONDON - The UK Airfreight Forum says the UK air cargo industry is aiming to establish agreed performance standards by the end of this year.
* BA chief executive Bob Ayling says it alliance with American Airlines would allow its competitors to access a $1.0 billion slice of the pair's existing revenues.
HONG KONG - Cathay says it completed the latest part of its fleet modernisation programme with the arrival in Hong Kong of its newest aircraft from Airbus.

PARIS - Singapore Airlines says it planned to introduce two, additional weekly Boeing 747-200 freighter flights between Paris/CDG to Singapore, in conjunction with Air France, effective end-March 1997, instead of one as initially planned.
* SIA says it will increase ex-Paris cargo rates to Singapore and selected onward destinations by around five percent, effective next April 1.
* Air France Europe says while it carried less airfreight in 1996 it did improve cargo yields.
FRANKFURT - Nippon Cargo Airlines says it is considering adding extra freighter flights from Japan to south-east Asia, Europe and the U.S. from this summer.
* Nippon says it has no short-term plans for any ex-Japan cargo rates rises or cuts.
MILAN - Schenker Italiana Spa says it has moved to new premises at Bandiera, Peschiera Borrmeo in northern Italy.
FRANKFURT - FedEx says it has appointed Peter Grimm as managing director sales for Germant and Eastern Europe.

NEW YORK - American Airlines and China Eastern Airlines says they had signed a memorandum of understanding to create reciprocal code-sharing programmes between American's service points in the U.S. and China Eastern's gateways of Beijing and Shanghai.
LONDON - The UK Airfreight Forum says it has agreed to cooperate on establishing an industry training scheme.
LONDON - Airlines officials says nine major airlines are forming a powerful new global alliance to counter the threat posed by the proposed link-up between BA and American Airlines.
LONDON - Virgin Atlantic says it is lifting air cargo rates from the UK by between 3 and 7 percent from April 1, depending on the prevailing market strengths of the routes.
LONDON - Cathay Pacific, UK air cargo manager, Mark Olney says it will raise its ex-UK air cargo rates by an average of five percent from April 1.
NEW YORK - The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey says it approved a lease for DHL Airways, expanding the carrier's operations at JFK.
* The authority says Northwest Airlines will build a $31 million air cargo complex at Kennedy airport under an authorized lease agreement.
LONDON - Lufthansa Cargo says the UK unit will in future attempto to give shippers and agents 30 days' notice of any fuel surcharges imposed.
LONDON - BA says a report that rivals were planning to strength their ties to create a single global network served only to strengthen the case for its proposed deal with American Airlines.
WASHINGTON - A key U.S. government official poured cold water on the possibility that nine major airlines could form a powerful new global alliance.
LONDON - United Airlines encouraged U.S. and Japanese transportation authorities to approve pending applications for air service.
ST.LOUIS - TWA says its board elected Gerald Gitner as chairman and CEO.
NEW YORK - Analysts says a sweeping network being formed by nine airlines will pose little threat to rival carriers since it merely adds to an already powerful alliance.
**FEBRUARY 13**
COPENHAGEN - SAS declined to confirm whether or not it had plans to participate in a new nine-airline global alliance.
AMSTERDAM - Cathay's Dutch manager Achim van der Graaff says it will be one of the first carriers introducing rates increases ex-Amsterdam from March 1.
TAIPEI - EVA Airways says Taiwan will begin commercial flights to Cambodia by the end of next month, despite protests from arch rival China.
LONDON - BAA says air cargo tonnage handled at BAA's seven British airport last month at 112,018 tonnes was 7.6 percent above the total for January 1996.
LISBON - Portuguese airline TAP spokeswoman says top-selling U.S. author Michael Crichton has apologised over a reference to a company he calls "Air Portugal" in his latest thriller.
JOHANNESBURG - SAA denied reports it was one of nine airlines planning an alliance to counter the threat of a proposed linkup between BA and American Airlines.
FRANKFURT - Lufthansa says its cargo freight unit had agreed to cooperate with SAS cargo, starting with joint sales operations.
LONDON - Lufthansa UK and Ireland director Bob Bingley says it will increase its ex-UK cargo rates by an across-the-board average of five percent from April 1.
AMSTERDAM - Schiphol airport saw total freight handled in January rise to 85,000 tonnes, an increase of 2.9 percent over the same month last year.
LONDON - Supermarket chain Tesco says it is preparing to beat the Spanish lorry blockade by flying food into Britain.
LONDON - Unisys Corp says that it has been awarded a contract to deliver a mobile data collection solution for Cargo Centre Copenhagen, the second largest ground handling agent in Copenhagen.
LONDON - AEI says it recorded a net income for 1996 of $38.5 million, up 33 percent on 1995.
HONG KONG - Qantas says it is to double its flights into China from two to four per week because of increasing passenger demand.
COPENHAGEN - SAS says that any extension if its present alliance with four other carriers would not alter the shape of the carrier's present proprietorship.
JERUSALEM - Israel's transport ministry proposed to float the government's entire shareholding in El-Al airlines in the domestic market but says the carrier must stay grounded on the Jewish sabbath.
LONDON - The UK's Manchester airport says airlines will launch new services this year on routes to New York, Istanbul, Lisbon and Oporto.
ISTANBUL - Hava-ls officials says the opening round of talks between Turkey's state airline Turk Hava Yollari and the trade union Have-ls ended without agreement.
LONDON, The UK's Manchester airport said airlines will launch new services this year on routes to New York, Istanbul, Lisbon and Oporto.
Delta Air Lines will start a daily scheduled Lockheed Tristar service to New York's JFK from June 2, departing at 13.00, the airport said in a statement.
A three times a week Boeing 737-400 service by Turkish Airlines between Manchester and Istanbul will begin on June 15.

JERUSALEM, Israel's Transport Ministry proposed on Thursday to float the government's entire shareholding in El Al airlines in the domestic market but said the carrier must stay grounded on the Jewish sabbath.
ISTANBUL, The opening round of talks between Turkey's state airline Turk Hava Yollari (THY) and the trade union Hava-Is ended without agreement on Thursday, Hava-Is officials said.
PARIS - French champagne growers fighting plans to lay high-speed TGV rail lines near their vines have commissioned a study which shows the project could trap cold air and endanger their harvest.
HONG KONG - Feb 13(Reuter)- Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said the airline carried 2.5 percent more passengers and 8.6 percent more cargo in December 1996 compared to the same month in 1995.

BUDAPEST - Hungary's government commissioned Privatisation Minister Judit Csiha to work out by April 30 a plan for the privatisation of the national air carrier Malev, a government spokesman said on Thursday.
ISTANBUL - The opening round of talks between Turkey's state airline Turk Hava Yollari (THY) and the trade union Hava-Is ended without agreement on Thursday, Hava-Is officials said.

LODZ - Poland plans to convert and expand a military airfield near the central city of Lodz into a cargo airport which could start operating late next year, an official at Lodz's governor office said on Thursday.
WASHINGTON - American Airlines Chairman Robert Crandall said Thursday that he was unsure that a strike by the airline's pilots could be avoided.
* American Airlines Thursday rejected an offer by its pilots to compromise on the contentious issue of who will fly the carrier's new regional jet planes.
*Crandall said arbitration may be needed to avert a strike threatened by the airline's pilots.
FRANKFURT-Lufthansa Cargo AG will take over freight handling of SAS Cargo at Frankfurt Airport from May, an SAS official said.
HONG KONG-Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said the airline carried 2.5 percent more passengers and 8.6 percent more cargo in December 1996 compared to the same month in 1995.

TOULOUSE- European aircraft consortium Airbus expects to make a decision on its planned large plane which would seat 550 passengers towards the end of 1998 or 1999, managing director Jean Pierson said on Thursday.

COPENHAGEN-Analysts expect Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) to more or less match its own forecast of a fall in 1996 pre-tax profits to 1.74 billion Swedish crowns from 1995's 2.63 billion when its publishes its annual accounts on Monday.

BASLE-Freight forwarder Danzas AG said its board of directors had agreed to simplify the capital structure and use resulting cash for an extraordinary payment to shareholders of 26.2 million Swiss francs.
FRANKFURT-Lufthansa Cargo AG said its new cargo co-operation with SAS Cargo is a first step to full global cargo co-operation.

CHICAGO-The ratings on AMR Corp'sspecial facility municipal revenue debt, issued for airport projects, may be reviewed for possible downgrade if pilots strike AMR's American Airlines, according to analysts from Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's Corp.
LONDON-The index of future U.S. air cargo business dropped 0.3 percent to 528.0 in December, compared to a 0.2 percent gain in November, the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi said. Board since Monday.
FRANKFURT-ufthansa Cargo AG said its new cargo co-operation with SAS Cargo is a first step to full global cargo co-operation.
WASHINGTON-The American Airlines pilots' union said it would welcome President Bill Clinton's help in trying to avert a pending strike, although the pilots remained opposed to binding arbitration.
AALSMEER-Pre-Valentine's Day trading at the world's largest flower auction at Aalsmeer has been fast and furious, auction spokeswoman Adrienne Langsbergen told Reuters.
LONDON-British retailer Marks & Spencer plc has halted food and textile exports from the UK to Spain because of the Spanish truckers strike, a Marks & Spencer spokewoman said.

WASHINGTON-A key issue in the dispute is whether American Airlines can fly the small jets of its regional carrier, American Eagle, with lower-paid pilots belonging to another union, a move opposed by the Allied Pilots Association.
* An American Airlines pilots union spokesman said Thursday "we're not that far apart" on terms for a new contract which would avert a strike scheduled for midnight Friday.
MIAMI-Freight forwarders shipping to Latin America have already begun keeping their freight off American Airlines to avoid any problems in case American's pilots strike, executives told Reuters.
NEW YORK-The price of jet fuel in the United States will probably slump sharply if pilots of American Airlines carry out a threatened strike at midnight Friday, industry executives said.
LONDON-European jet fuel premiums to gas oil futures were a touch weaker on Wednesday, despite heavy swaps buying.
WASHINGTON-President Bill Clinton remains convinced that AMR Corp and its pilots should use federal mediation to resolve their dispute, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said .
NAPLES-The city of Naples said a deal in which British airport operator BAA Plc is set to buy a 65 percent in the city's Capodichino airport would be signed "in the next few days."
NEW YORK-American Airlines ould survive a pilot strike of about 42 days before falling into the red for the year, but most industry analysts expect the threatened strike to last less than a week.

GUATEMALA CITY-Guatemala's state-owned railway, telecommunications, electricity, post office, tourism office and airports will be sold or drastically restructured this year, the government's privatization czar said Thursday.
BUENOS AIRES-Argentina may be ready to privatize its main airports by July, President Carlos Menem said Thursday.
PARIS-French Industry Minister Franck Borotra said in a newspaper interview he wanted the procedure for privatising electronics group Thomson CSF to "be transparent."
WASHINGTON-President Clinton is "seriously considering" becoming involved in the American Airlines labor dispute with its pilots, Rep. Martin Frost, D-Texas, said Thursday.
NEW YORK-World Airways Inc said Thursday it had 3,853 block hurs flown from continuing operations in January, up 23 percent from 3,131 in January 1996.
DENVER-If American Airlines pilots go on strike Friday, it ould not come at a worse time for Colorado's famed ski resorts, officials said.

NEW YORK - A strike by pilots of AMR Corp could wreak havoc on Dade County, Fla.'s economy, costing it about $400 million over 30 days, county mayor Alex Penelas said Thursday on cable television station CNBC.

LONDON - British Airways Engineering said it has signed a contract with FLA Aerospace Ltd to supply aircraft maintenance services at London's Gatwick airport, Manchester and Stansted from March 1997 to October 2000.
HUNTINGTON BEACH - McDonnell Douglas and Loral Space & Communications Ltd unit Space Systems/Loral said Thursday they entered into an agreement for five Delta III launches between 1999 and 2001.

DALLAS - Jittery passengers of American Airlines scrambled Thursday to save their travel plans for the long Presidents Day weekend as rival carriers looked to take advantage of American's looming pilots strike.
MINNEAPOLIS - Northwest Airlines Corp said Thursday that it is prepared to accept tickets for AMR Corp's American Airlines from passengers affected by a possible strike by American's pilots.
WASHINGTON - A strike by American Airlines Inc pilots could cost the U.S. economy between $100 and $200 million a day, a senior Department of Transportation official said Thursday.

LONDON-British Airways Engineering said it has signed a contract with FLA Aerospace Ltd to supply aircraft maintenance services at London's Gatwick airport, Manchester and Stansted from March 1997 to October 2000.

TAMPA, Fla-British Aerospace Holdings Inc and Reflectone Inc said on Thursday that they have signed a merger agreement in which British Aerospace will buy the remaining common stock of Reflectone at $24 per share.
MIAMI - Any walkout by American Airlines pilots would hit tourist-dependent Caribbean islands like a hurricane, while Latin America's diversified economies should easily weather a service-stoppage.
**FRIDAY FEBRUARY 14**

LONDON - An investigation has been launched into the new generation of superjet used by British Airways after one began to roll mysteriously and had to return to London's Heathrow airport, the Independent newspaper said on Friday.
WASHINGTON - President Clinton said Friday a pilots strike at American Airlines would be "quite disruptive" to air travel and urged the parties to reach out to each other.

WASHINGTON - U.S. Defense Secretary William Cohen said Thursday small U.S. business firms received $25.3 billion in prime defense contract awards in fiscal 1996, a record 23.7 pct of military funding awarded by the Pentagon.
WASHINGTON - Pilots of American Airlines will make a comprehensive proposal later Thursday to try to end a dispute with the company and head off a strike, a union leader said.
NEW YORK - The price of jet fuel in the United States will probably slump sharply if pilots of American Airlines carry out a threatened strike at midnight Friday, industry executives said.
JOHANNESBURG - Virgin Atlantic Airways announced on Friday that it would double the number of flights on its London-Johannesburg route to six flights a week in each direction from March 1.

NEW YORK - The Justice Department has extended for another month its antitrust review of Raytheon's proposed $3 billion acquisition of Texas Instruments' defense business, the Wall Street Journal said Friday.
NEW YORK - The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey said
it formally finalised a lease agreement with Korean Airlines for a $105 million air cargo hub at JFK.
AMSTERDAM - Heavy air cargo traffic in flowers for Valentine's Day was the key feature in a market awaiting rate increase to come into effect in March, a Reuters survey showed.
LONDON - Shares in British airport operator BAA Plc fell on Friday on reports that a windfall tax planned by the opposition Labour Party would apply to the company, dealers said.
SINGAPORE - Asian airlines, bruised by rises in jet fuel prices, are poised for a comfortable ride after the market took a beating this week, industry sources said on Friday.

LONDON - Airfreight trading from the UK to North and Latin America is in a healthy state despite the traditional off-peak season for the industry and at a time when sterling continues to strengthen, a Reuters survey shows.

LONDON - Racal Electronics Plc unit said on Friday that its Racal Avionics unit is to buy British Airways' Aerad flight navigation information business for "in the region of five million stg" in cash.
HONG KONG - South African Airways] is due to start a fourth weekly frequency between Johannesburg and Hong Kong on February 15, an airline spokeswoman said.

HELSINKI - Finnish national carrier Finnair Oy said on Friday it had sold three DC-10 aircrafts to Capra Corporation and would book a 40 million markka profit for the first plane in its report for the year to March 31, 1997.
WASHINGTON - A strike by American Airlines Incpilots could cost the U.S. economy between $100 and $200 million a day, a senior Department of Transportation official said Thursday.
CHICAGO - Billions of dollars of AMR Corp's municipal debt could be affected by a pilots strike against American Airlines, according to bond rating agencies.
LAGOS - Nigeria's aviation ministry cancelled a 200 percent increase in local air fares announced by airline operators.
AMSTERDAM - A KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV Cargo spokesman said the Dutch airline is making more space available on its flights to Spain due to the worsening Spanish truckers strike.
HAIKOU - For Chen Feng, chairman and president of the Chinese regional carrier Hainan Airlines, a woman's place is on board -- and not in the boardroom.

LONDON - British airports operator BAA Plc said on Firday it was confident it would not be hit by the opposition Labour Party's proposed windfall tax, despite a new report that said it had new evidence that BAA would be liable.
MADRID - Spain's agriculture sector has lost about 20 billion pesetas so far in a nine-day-old truckers strike, the farmers' cooperative CCAE estimated on Friday.
WOLFSBURG - German carmaker Volkswagen AG said on Friday that workers at the group's main plant in Wolfsburg would work shortened shifts from Saturday because of transport strikes in Spain.
LONDON - Rescue services said on Friday they were trying to recover between 20 and 30 containers lost overboard from a cargo ship off Britain's southwest coast.
MIAMI - Greenwich Air Services Inc said Friday it had reached a definitive agreement to merge with UNC Inc in a deal worth no less than $320 million.

COPENHAGEN - Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS)said it has been the openly declared ambition of it and its foreign partners (Lufthansa, United Airlines, Thai Airways International and Air Canada) to deepen their alliances but did not give further details.
PARIS - French road hauliers denounced striking Spanish truckers on Friday and blamed an atmosphere of violence "close to insurrection" for the death of a Spanish picket run over by a French trucker.
